correctness.summary: For each length k, the deterministic alphabet cap gives the lower deficit. The upper deficit is bounded by equal substring pairs; two distinct length-k windows match with probability exactly d^{-k}, including overlapping windows because a shift-s match leaves s free symbols in a block of k+s letters. Summing at m=floor(log_d n) gives matching n log_d n leading terms. Exhaustive finite enumeration for binary n<=16 and ternary n<=10 confirms the stated sandwich.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Godbole (2026) studies the same all-length expectation but gives weaker logarithmic-loss constants; Flaxman-Harrow-Sorkin (2004) establish only n^2-scale asymptotic optimality in the inspected random-string comparison; Ahmadi-Ward (2020) analyze individual kth-level profiles. Searches did not locate the coefficient-one all-length correction, the finite collision sandwich, or the explicit O(n) additive gap to the maximum. Older suffix-tree/trie path-length literature remains a residual risk of equivalent implicit coverage.

value.summary: The theorem identifies the sharp first correction beyond the quadratic leading term, improves the recent all-length bounds, and shows that uniform random words are additively O(n) from the extremal distinct-substring count. The proof is elementary and finite-sample, isolating exact overlap collision probabilities rather than requiring Poisson approximation.

limitations: The alphabet size d is fixed and the letters are uniform and independent.
The O_d(n) second-order term is not identified.
No extension to general nonuniform memoryless sources is claimed.
No variance or concentration result for D_n is proved.
Older suffix-tree/trie path-length literature remains a residual originality risk.
Cross-model review has not been performed.
